1.why: All four close the same quoted phrase; the only one that closes an opened parenthesis without adding an unneeded comma or dash is the bare ')'.

2.why: Classic dangling-modifier set: only B supplies a human agent ('conservators') as the subject; A, C and D all begin with a thing or expletive.

3.why: Two options keep 'in' and two drop it; the comma-plus-preposition version is the one that closes a nonrestrictive element correctly.

4.why: Present-perfect plural is the unmarked choice against a future-perfect and a past-progressive distractor pair.

5.why: Infinitive is the parallel/complement form; the noun and finite-clause options are the usual wrong-form distractors.

6.why: Stem's singular verb 'took' forces singular 'work', and the following appositive is already opened by a comma, so the comma version pairs with it.

7.why: Pure punctuation ladder (semicolon/none/comma/colon); comma is the default supplement boundary with no clause or list signalled.

8.why: 'By the time ... signed' in the stem sets a past reference point, so past perfect 'had fought' is required.

9.why: Only C's content ('long after the artist's death') supplies the time relation such completion items normally hinge on; the others are freestanding facts.

10.why: Colon introducing a noun-phrase appositive; A adds 'that', C's 'such as:' is ungrammatical, D mismatches dash with semicolon.

11.why: 'which' is the only relative pronoun that can open a nonrestrictive clause; 'it' and 'and it' would splice or restart.

12.why: Two independent clauses ('clarity' ends one, 'astronomers' starts another): semicolon is the only legal joiner among fused, comma-splice and unpunctuated-and options.

13.why: 'on hand' completes an independent clause introducing a list, so the colon is right; the other three fuse, over-punctuate, or insert a stray verb.

14.why: Full case ladder (she/hers/herself/her); the objective form is the most commonly keyed in this shape.

15.why: Singular present against past, present-perfect and plural distractors.

16.why: Same four-form agreement ladder as 15 with letters rotated; singular present again.

17.why: Plural present 'are' — the have/has pair are auxiliary distractors and 'were' shifts tense needlessly.

18.why: Counterfactual conditional wants 'would have been damped'; A is tense-short, B drops the conditional, D flips to active with a stray particle.

19.why: 'lie/lay' set — past perfect 'had lain' is the correct intransitive form and the only one that anchors to a prior past.

20.why: Infinitive complement; gerund, bare past and finite clause are the standard wrong-form trio.

21.why: Same to-infinitive/gerund/finite/noun quartet as 5 and 20; infinitive is the parallel form.

22.why: Dangling-modifier set again: only A names an animate agent ('the research team') able to perform the introductory action.

23.why: Stem's delayed subject 'several complaints' is plural, so 'were'.

24.why: Fourth instance of the infinitive-vs-gerund-vs-finite ladder; 'to present' is the parallel form.
